prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: side impact at intersection in Baytown, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck and back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1174; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officers responded to a report of a side-impact collision at an intersection in Baytown, Texas. Driver 1 was proceeding through the intersection when the front of Driver 2's vehicle struck the driver's side of Driver 1's vehicle. Driver 2 stated that the collision occurred as described by Driver 1, and two independent witnesses gave consistent accounts of the impact and the position of both vehicles. Scene photographs were taken and show damage to the driver's side of Driver 1's vehicle that corresponds with the direction and force of the impact. Passenger was seated in the front passenger seat of Driver 1's vehicle at the time of the crash, a fact confirmed by Driver 1, Driver 2, and the witnesses. Driver 1 reported neck and back pain at the scene and was evaluated by responding personnel, with symptoms consistent with the forces involved. No prior damage to Driver 1's vehicle was observed or reported. Driver 1 is listed as a named insured on the policy covering the vehicle involved. No citations were issued at the scene pending further review of the collision.
